dedupe_keys.name: usda ers food security in the united states current population survey food security supplement

description: The Current Population Survey Food Security Supplement is the annual U.S. household survey that measures whether households had enough food during the year. Its public-use files give each household's answers to the food security module, its food security status, food spending and use of food assistance such as the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, WIC and food pantries, linked to demographic data from the Current Population Survey. The producer is the Economic Research Service of the U.S. Department of Agriculture, which sponsors and analyses the supplement, with the U.S. Census Bureau, which runs the survey and releases the household data. Coverage is national, with state estimates from pooled years, annually since 1995. Files are public-use microdata with questionnaires and user notes, free to download; as federal statistics they carry no licence restrictions. Caveats: the survey asks about the past year, so short disruptions are blurred; people outside households are not sampled; and state estimates need several years pooled. Simulation uses: household vulnerability baselines and observed responses to shocks for validating models of food supply disruption, food bank demand and emergency food distribution. Related records: the USDA Food Access Research Atlas (data-usda-ers-food-access-research-atlas) gives the geography of store access.
